answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to register through a hardware-attested inlet: the agent identity key must be generated inside a trusted execution environment and bound to one physical device, so one machine yields exactly one credential. An attacker wanting a plume of fake agents must buy a new device for every identity, turning a free software trick into a per-identity hardware cost. Peers then mirror that attestation on-chain, and any duplicate device fingerprint revokes every identity tied to it.
